note.note:
History:
- Chief complaint: Reduced hearing in the left ear.
- Onset/duration: ~6 weeks; intermittent course.
- Associated symptoms: Left-sided ringing (tinnitus), intermittent mild dizziness/off-balance (not true spinning vertigo; minimal/no nausea).
- Triggers: Watching TV/listening to music can bring on ringing.
- Laterality: Left ear only; right ear seems normal per patient.
- Pain/fever/discharge: No ear pain; no discharge; no fever specifically reported.
- Cardiopulmonary: Chest pain denied; palpitations not recorded.
- Prior episodes: Brief similar episode about a year ago lasting a couple of days.
- Ear care: Denies using cotton buds/Q-tips.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic illnesses: Not discussed.
- Allergies: Not discussed.
- Medications: Not discussed.
- Prior surgeries/hospitalizations: Not discussed.
- Family/social history (including noise exposure): Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- Video visit; no vitals obtained.
- No in-person otoscopic exam performed yet.
- Other exam findings: Not recorded.

Impression:
- Unilateral left hearing difficulty with intermittent tinnitus and mild imbalance for 6 weeks; etiology undetermined pending otoscopic evaluation.
- Differential diagnoses (consistent with transcript):
  - Cerumen impaction causing conductive hearing loss and tinnitus—common, painless; needs exclusion by otoscopy.
  - Eustachian tube dysfunction/otitis media with effusion—can cause fluctuating unilateral hearing change with tinnitus; no pain/fever supports possibility.
  - Early Ménière disease—unilateral tinnitus and fluctuating hearing with episodic imbalance; lacks classic spinning vertigo/aural fullness.

Management Plan:
- Arrange face-to-face clinic visit within 4–5 days for otoscopic examination to assess for wax/physical blockage and inspect the tympanic membrane.
- Provide tinnitus patient-education leaflet link; patient to review before the visit.
- Avoid inserting cotton buds/Q-tips or other objects into the ear.
- Safety-net: If symptoms worsen, new neurological symptoms develop, or concerns arise before the appointment, book another urgent video appointment. Not an emergency currently per clinician.
- Administrative: Clinician to notify admin to schedule; patient to call support team number to secure appointment slot.

Patient Summary:
- Patient reports 6 weeks of intermittent left-sided hearing reduction with tinnitus and mild imbalance, without pain or discharge, and a brief prior episode a year ago. Plan is prompt in-person ear exam to rule out cerumen impaction or other otologic causes and to review tinnitus information ahead of follow-up.

Key Takeaways:
- Attend the in-person ear check within 4–5 days.
- Read the tinnitus leaflet to understand symptoms and available management options.
- Do not use cotton buds/Q-tips to clean the ear.

Next Steps:
- Complete scheduled otoscopic exam.
- Subsequent management to be decided based on exam findings (e.g., wax removal if present or further evaluation as indicated).

Quality checks:
- Missing elements: Past medical history, medication list, allergies, vitals, detailed ROS (aural fullness, recent URI/allergy symptoms, noise exposure, ototoxic medications), response to palpitations question, ear itchiness.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted. Fever response somewhat unclear (“not specifically”); DDx assumes afebrile—appears consistent.
- Transcript quality: Minor gaps/inaudible portions and transcription artifacts; some questions unanswered or unclear.
